question: Explain what a load balancer is and describe different load balancing algorithms. When would you use each?

keyPoints: Load balancer distributes incoming requests across multiple servers to improve availability and performance
Round-robin: cycles through servers equally, simple but doesn't consider server load
Least connections: routes to server with fewest active connections, good for long-lived connections
Weighted algorithms consider server capacity; IP hash ensures same client goes to same server
Health checks ensure traffic only goes to healthy servers
expectedAnswer.explanation: Load balancers are critical for horizontal scaling and high availability. Round-robin works for stateless applications with similar request processing times. Least connections is better when requests have variable duration (e.g., file uploads). IP hash maintains session affinity without sticky sessions. Modern load balancers operate at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP) or Layer 7 (HTTP), with Layer 7 offering more intelligent routing based on request content.
